meta.title: Romanian C2 Proficiency
meta.subtitle: 1,500 more words, none of them in A1 to C1 · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Romanian → English (see the Romanian, recall the meaning) and English → Romanian (see an English meaning, recall the Romanian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1500 words for a proficient learner, aligned to C2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand with ease virtually everything heard or read' — a learner here is able to summarise information from different spoken and written sources, reconstructing arguments and accounts in a coherent presentation, and to express themselves spontaneously, very fluently and precisely, differentiating finer shades of meaning even in more complex situations. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be — no openly licensed graded word list for Romanian was found to build it from. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 538 of the 1500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — the literary and elevated vocabulary of written Romanian, the older words still alive in its literature, rhetoric and style, history, faith and tradition, the countryside and its crafts, law, administration and scholarship at their most formal, the finest shades of character, feeling and judgement, precise verbs of speech, sight, movement and manner, and the rarer adjectives and adverbs that separate a fluent speaker from a precise one — and the other 962 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Romanian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every form of a noun or a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword carries its pronunciation in the International Phonetic Alphabet, Wiktionary's own, because Romanian does not write where the stress falls. Verbs are given in the dictionary's form, with the infinitive's a (a face, to do). The 872 nouns show their gender — masculine, feminine or neuter, the neuter being masculine in the singular and feminine in the plural — their plural, and their definite form, the article being a suffix (casă, a house; casa, the house); the 223 verbs show their first person, past participle and subjunctive, and behind the All forms fold their present, imperfect, subjunctive and imperative by person. Real example sentences come with 617 of the 1500 words, three apiece for 196 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, gender, forms and pronunciation: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.

fields.Examples:
Într-un articol recent despre activități care să-ți antreneze mintea, se menționează Esperanto precum și Sudoku, ceea ce denotă ca Esperanto devine parte a culturii de masă.
In a recent article about activities to keep your brain young, they mention Esperanto along with Sudoku, which shows that Esperanto is becoming part of popular culture.
Asta poate fi datorită unei schimbări a atitudinii publicului față de căsătorie, precum și a creșterii vertiginoase a localurilor de tip fast food și a magazinelor mici, deschise 24 de ore și care oferă tinerilor un trai mai lejer.
This may be because of a change in people's attitude toward marriage and the sharp increase of fast food restaurants and convenience stores which are open 24 hours a day and enable young people to live more easily.
